definitions.explanation: Having the color of blood or a ripe tomato.

examples.japanese: {赤|あか}い⟦{花|はな}→花：00523_hana⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦きれい→きれい：00717_kirei⟧⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。
{赤|あか}い⟦{車|くるま}→車：00516_kuruma⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}いました→買う：00489_kau⟧。
⟦りんご→りんご：02269_ringo⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{赤|あか}く⟦なりました→なる：01970_naru⟧。⟦{食|た}べられます→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: The apples have turned red. They're ready to eat.

examples.japanese: ⟦{信号|しんごう}→信号：03258_shingou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{赤|あか}い⟦です→です：09485_desu⟧。⟦{青|あお}→青：02841_ao⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦なったら→なる：01970_naru⟧、⟦{渡|わた}れます→渡る：02441_wataru⟧。
examples.english: The light is red. When it turns green, you can cross.

notes:
USAGE:
{赤|あか}い works both before a noun ({赤|あか}い⟦{車|くるま}→車：00516_kuruma⟧) and as a predicate (⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{赤|あか}い). It covers a wider range of shades than English "red," reaching into orange and pink: ripe fruit, a sunset, and a flushed face are all {赤|あか}い.

FORMS:
- Noun form: ⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧ (the color red)
- Adverbial: {赤|あか}く ({赤|あか}く⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧ = to become red)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{顔|かお}→顔：00558_kao⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{赤|あか}く⟦なる→なる：01970_naru⟧: to blush, to turn red (from embarrassment or anger)
- ⟦{赤|あか}ちゃん→赤ちゃん：01282_akachan⟧: baby (literally "red one" — newborns look reddish)
- ⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{他人|たにん}→他人：01459_tanin⟧: complete stranger
- ⟦{赤字|あかじ}→赤字：04712_akaji⟧: deficit, "in the red"
- ⟦{赤信号|あかしんごう}→赤信号：21543_akashingou⟧: red light

The last three take the noun ⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧, not the adjective. Set compounds of this kind normally use the noun form, so a traffic light is ⟦{赤信号|あかしんごう}→赤信号：21543_akashingou⟧ rather than {赤|あか}い⟦{信号|しんごう}→信号：03258_shingou⟧, though the adjective is fine in a full sentence (⟦{信号|しんごう}→信号：03258_shingou⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{赤|あか}い).

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {赤|あか}い: red
- ⟦{青|あお}い→青い：00586_aoi⟧: blue — but also "green" for traffic lights and fresh leaves
- ⟦{黄色|きいろ}い→黄色い：00959_kiiroi⟧: yellow
- ⟦{黒|くろ}い→黒い：00588_kuroi⟧: black

CULTURAL NOTE:
Red symbolizes celebration and good fortune in Japan. ⟦{紅白|こうはく}→紅白：13805_kouhaku⟧ (red and white) is the standard festive pairing, used for everything from ceremonial curtains to the New Year's Eve song contest.
